diagnostic_evidence.quote: Consequently, the entire transformed integrand is bounded near the boundary.
under specific "QMC-friendly" growth conditions on the integrand and its derivatives

issues.failure_explanation: The derived boundary growth conditions only make the ratio r = (characteristic function)/(proposal density) bounded, so the transformed integrand g~ stays bounded near the corners. The paper itself says the O(N^{-1+eps}) rate needs growth conditions on the integrand AND its (mixed) derivatives, plus corner-avoiding points. No derivative bound, Hardy-Krause variation estimate, or rate theorem is established for g~. Bounded integrands can still have infinite Hardy-Krause variation or badly growing mixed derivatives. The 'ensure nearly optimal rates' and 'preserves sufficient regularity' statements therefore rest only on 1D/low-d numerical evidence.

failure_location.quote: we tune the parameters of the proposal density to satisfy the derived boundary growth conditions that ensure nearly optimal convergence rates

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Reword the claim as a necessary/heuristic boundedness condition supported by experiments, or prove Owen-type derivative growth bounds for g~ under the chosen proposals.
issues.overall_effect: The central methodological guarantee (conditions in Tables 3-4 yield nearly optimal RQMC convergence) is unproven; only boundedness is shown. The dimension-independent claims of 'optimal rates' are empirical.
issues.title: Boundedness of the transformed integrand is presented as ensuring nearly optimal RQMC rates
issues.why_classification: The fix is either a contained weakening of the wording or a new derivative-bound lemma. The practical recipe and experiments remain intact, so this is more than local but not a loss of the whole method.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: is a common gamma process with parameters
is a common inverse Gaussian process with parameters

issues.failure_explanation: In the Appendix the multivariate VG and NIG models share one gamma/inverse-Gaussian time change across all assets, so the joint characteristic function (1 - i nu z'theta + (nu/2) z'Sigma z)^{-T/nu} (resp. exp(-delta T sqrt(z'Delta z))) does not factor into marginals, even for diagonal Sigma or Delta = I. The paper's own dependent-case analysis then requires tilde nu = 2T/nu - d for VG and a multivariate Laplace with tilde Sigma = (2/(delta^2 T^2)) Delta^{-1} for NIG. Yet the d>1 experiments use the univariate rules (tilde nu = 2T/nu - 1 = 9 for d = 4; product-Laplace with tilde sigma = 1/(delta T) or sqrt(2)/(delta T)). For NIG the product-Laplace exponent is ||y||_1 while the characteristic function decays like exp(-delta T ||y||_2). Along diagonal directions the ratio therefore grows exponentially unless tilde sigma >= sqrt(d)/(delta T). For VG the product-t density decays like rho^{-d(tilde nu+1)} against rho^{-2T/nu}. So the experiments for d>1 do not satisfy the paper's own boundary growth conditions.

failure_location.quote: We considered the case in which the underlying assets are independent; hence, the multivariate characteristic function can be factored into the product of the univariate characteristic functions

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either apply the dependent-asset rules (tilde nu = 2T/nu - d; multivariate Laplace/t with the prescribed tilde Sigma) in the d>1 experiments, or define VG/NIG with genuinely independent components. Alternatively, justify the product proposals via payoff decay.
issues.overall_effect: The multi-asset VG/NIG numerical results (Figs. 4D basket, 3D/6D, up to 15D runtime comparisons) are not backed by the stated conditions. Their good behaviour would have to come from payoff-transform decay, which is not analysed.
issues.title: 'Independent assets' VG/NIG rules conflict with the common-subordinator models actually used in the experiments
issues.why_classification: The correct rules are already in the paper, but the experiments must be re-run or re-justified. The theory-to-experiment linkage for VG/NIG is affected, not the whole method.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: which, if not satisfied, implies that the characteristic function is not integrable

issues.failure_explanation: The derived condition for VG is tilde nu <= 2T/nu - 1; case (i), tilde nu > 2T/nu - 1, gives an unbounded ratio. The summary recommends tilde nu = nu_bar + epsilon with epsilon >= 0, which lies on or in the forbidden side (the multivariate case correctly uses minus). For 2T/nu - 1 < 0 the Remark prescribes tilde nu = max(2T/nu - 1, 1) = 1, which violates tilde nu <= 2T/nu - 1 < 0, and no tilde nu > 0 can satisfy the condition. The paper gives no replacement argument for this regime beyond a later informal remark that payoff decay may help.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace + by - in the summary. For 2T/nu - 1 <= 0, state that the condition cannot be met and give an argument (using payoff-transform decay) for a valid tilde nu, or restrict the scope.
issues.overall_effect: The practical rule for choosing tilde nu in the univariate VG case is wrong for epsilon > 0 and unsupported for short maturities (small T/nu), a practically relevant regime.
issues.title: Univariate VG parameter recipe contradicts the stated boundary growth condition (sign of epsilon; short-maturity floor)
issues.why_classification: The sign is a quick fix, but the short-maturity regime needs a new contained argument or a scope restriction.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: By the monotonicity of $x \mapsto \log(x)$, selecting $\tilde{\nu} = \frac{2T }{\nu}-d$ results in the following:

issues.failure_explanation: With tilde nu = 2T/nu - d, h_1^VG is proportional to ((Psi^{-1})' tilde Sigma^{-1} Psi^{-1} / (Psi^{-1})' Sigma Psi^{-1})^{T/nu}. This ratio of two quadratic forms is bounded above and below by eigenvalue ratios and does not tend to infinity or zero as ||Psi^{-1}|| -> infinity. Hence case (i) does not give +infinity and case (iii) does not give 0; the limit is bounded (and generally does not exist). The ratio is bounded for every positive definite tilde Sigma, so the matrix condition Sigma - tilde Sigma^{-1} >= 0 is spurious. Only the choice of tilde nu relative to 2T/nu - d (as in eq:mvg_conditions_2) controls polynomial growth or decay. The logarithmic-difference argument incorrectly treats a bounded difference of logs as divergent.

failure_location.quote: Equation~\eqref{eq:mvg_dom_trans_cond} indicates that if $\tilde{\nu} = \frac{2T}{\nu} - d$, then three possible cases exist:

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate: for tilde nu = 2T/nu - d the ratio is bounded for any positive definite tilde Sigma; for tilde nu < 2T/nu - d it decays; otherwise it blows up. Then choose tilde Sigma only to minimise constants.
issues.overall_effect: The first alternative in the multivariate VG rule (tilde nu = 2T/nu - d with a matrix inequality on tilde Sigma) rests on false limit statements. The adopted choice tilde Sigma = Sigma^{-1} still gives a bounded ratio, but the stated conditions are not the correct characterisation.
issues.title: Multivariate VG boundary limits (+infinity / 0) are wrong because the ratio of quadratic forms is homogeneous of degree zero
issues.why_classification: A short local recomputation corrects the classification, and the recommended parameter choice and numerical conclusions survive unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: For the TP approach, only central processing unit (CPU) times of up to six dimensions are measured in Python, and the values for the remaining dimensions are numerically extrapolated.
In contrast, for the TP quadrature, the stopping criterion is based on the exact relative error.

issues.failure_explanation: The RQMC/MC statistical error is a 95% confidence half-width computed from S shifts. It is not a deterministic upper bound on the true error, and the 'exact' error is itself measured against an MC reference with its own error. Using this to call the comparison 'conservative' is unsupported. The TP baseline is stopped on a different (exact-error) criterion, and its cost for d > 6 is extrapolated rather than measured. Section 4 lists tested dimensions without 15, while the abstract and conclusions claim the advantage 'for options with up to 15 assets'.

failure_location.quote: Consequently, the statistical error of the MC and RQMC methods is an upper bound; thus, the CPU times for the MC and RQMC methods are conservative

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use the same error criterion for all methods, state that the confidence half-width is probabilistic, and report TP costs as extrapolations. Align the stated tested dimensions with the 15-asset claim.
issues.overall_effect: The headline claims of speed-ups of about 100x and superiority over TP up to 15 assets are not established on a like-for-like basis.
issues.title: Runtime comparison claims rest on extrapolated TP costs, non-equivalent stopping criteria, and an invalid 'upper bound' argument
issues.why_classification: The numerical conclusions likely survive after re-stating the criterion and caveats; this is a local correction of the evaluation claims rather than of the method.
